The problem
Fact-checking Wikipedia is still manual.
Static banners and raw revision logs hide what editors actually need to see:
Silent Contradictions
Slow source and bias checks
Vague Transition Banners
Noisy Revision Logs
The solution
Four checks on every article. One card tells the editor what to fix.
Conflicts
Do editions contradict each other?
Compares linked language editions with Gemini to flag conflicting numbers, dates, and claims—and highlights them on the page.
Missing here
What is this edition missing?
Uses semantic comparison and Gemini to surface important facts and sections other languages cover that this page lacks.
Find Sources
What do neutral sources say?
MariaDB vector RAG + Verda return cited passages (today or as of any past date), with Gemini checking every source for neutrality.
Version History
How has the knowledge changed?
MariaDB system-versioned tables + Gemini Decisions trace claim shifts and edit wars down to the exact Wikipedia diff.
HOW WE SOLVED IT
One MariaDB database uniting Native Vector Search (RAG) and System-Versioned Tables (SVT)—paired with Gemini and Verda to turn raw Wikipedia text into instant editorial action.
Editor workflow
From any Wikipedia page to a verified edit. The editor stays in charge.
1
Open
Visit any Wikipedia article and open the WikiCheck extension.
2
Inspect
Review Conflicts, Missing here, Find sources, and Version history in one sidebar.
3
Verify and Fix
Click Show on the page to highlight the claim, check neutral sources, or jump to the exact diff.
4
Check Again
Edit Wikipedia, then click Check again to confirm the conflict or gap is resolved.
WHY READERS CARE
Every fix removes a wrong fact, fills a gap or adds a source, and every reader of that article sees it.

THE RESULT
  • On Hauho, WikiCheck shows the wrong area figure to fix first.
  • One glance at Hauho tells an editor what to fix first.
  • On Hauho, an editor immediately spots 3 conflicts and 4 missing sections.
Who benefits
Instant clarity for editors. More trustworthy articles for readers.
Editors
Spot cross-language conflicts, missing sections, uncited sources, and exact claim-changing diffs right inside the article—no more searching blind.
Readers
Fewer contradictions, missing facts, and biased wording—plus full transparency into how an article evolved over time.
Wikipedia
Smaller language editions catch up with better-covered ones, keeping knowledge consistent across languages.
WHAT WE CLAIM, AND WHAT WE DON’T
WikiCheck surfaces evidence—humans make the edit. Two editions agreeing isn't proof of truth, so we highlight conflicts, gaps, neutrality flags, and version shifts for editors to verify.
The stack
Open models, one API, MariaDB in the middle.
MariaDB Vector Search (RAG)
MariaDB System-Versioned Tables (SVT)
Google Gemini API & Decisions
Verda Inference (kimi-k3-1-pro)
THE MAIN IDEA
MariaDB unifies vector RAG, time-travel SQL, and caching in one database—while smart routing lets Gemini and Verda focus purely on high-value reasoning.
WikiCheck
Wikipedia, checked against itself.
What's next: Built language-agnostic on Wikidata + multilingual vectors—ready to scale from EN / FI / SV to all 300+ Wikipedia editions.
Built with: MariaDB (Vector RAG + System-Versioned Tables), Google Gemini API & Decisions, Verda Inference, FastAPI, and Chrome Extension.
